title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Members nothing references, and code kept alive only by other dead code
summary: Kotlin Jump 1.42.0 goes after the dead code every per-symbol counter misses: class members nothing references, fields the app parses and then drops, keys written and never read, catalog aliases no build file names, and whole islands of declarations that reference only each other. Every finding quoted here was verified by hand on a 6410 file project before it shipped.

highlights.title: Dead Islands
highlights.description: Two functions calling each other with no outside caller both look referenced, so both survive every scan. Find Dead Islands reports the whole group instead, and deletes it in one reviewed change with the stale imports included. On a 6410 file project: 22 islands, 52 declarations, 29 of them invisible to per-symbol counting. Every one was checked by hand, and every deletable one was actually deleted on a branch with a green build and test suite.

highlights.title: Members Nothing References
highlights.description: The largest tier of dead code left: public, internal and protected class members. A comparable tool reports 506 of them on this project with a measured 57% false-positive rate. This scan reports 92, each hand-verified, by counting any mention of the name anywhere as a use. A third verdict, could be private, covers members reached only from inside their own class.

highlights.title: Four More Things The Build Never Complains About
highlights.description: Fields of deserialized models nothing reads, Intent extras and preference keys nothing gets back, version catalog aliases no build file names, and event subscriptions nothing ever posts to. The catalog check is the first one here that reads the build rather than the code.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Fixes the version catalog reader ignoring module = "group:artifact", the form most catalogs are written in. On a catalog using it throughout, all 164 libraries were invisible and the catalog hover was silently blank.
Fixes catalog accessors resolving by prefix rather than by segment, so where foo and foo-bar both existed, libs.foo.bar counted as a reference to both.
Fixes the member scan's external guard matching the word anywhere on the declaration line: a Java parameter named external was enough to shield its method from the scan.
